_meta.title: Statutory federal income tax bracket schedules, 1913-2025
_meta.source: Tax Foundation income-tax-rates dataset (1913-2019), a compilation of IRS SOI Historical Table 23 and IRS Revenue Procedures rather than a source in its own right; IRS publishes no machine-readable ladder at bracket granularity, and Table 23 itself carries only the lowest and highest bracket of each year, 1913-2018; IRS Revenue Procedures 2018-57 through 2024-40 (2019-2025, curated); IRS SOI Historical Table 23 for the published top rate; FRED CPIAUCNS for the constant-dollar deflator

fields.top: top marginal rate as published (IRS SOI Historical Table 23 through 2018, IRS Revenue Procedures thereafter)
fields.sched_top: top marginal rate on the raw bracket schedule ladder (single filer)
fields.adj: non-null only in the twelve years where top and sched_top disagree
fields.nb: bracket count on the single-filer schedule
fields.s: brackets per filing status (single, mfj, mfs, hoh), null before that status existed

notes: Statutory is not effective. Nobody pays the top rate on their whole income, and the threshold it applies at has moved enormously.

Twelve years diverge between the published top rate and the schedule ladder top: 1923, 1929, 1940, 1946, 1947, 1948, 1949, 1950, 1968, 1969, 1970, 1981. Each carries a documented `adj` entry; see curated/bracket_adjustments.yaml.
mfj and mfs schedules do not exist before 1949; hoh does not exist before 1952. These are null, never a back-projected copy of the single schedule.
Excludes the alternative minimum tax, the phase-out of exemptions and deductions, and the 3.8% net investment income tax from 2013.

deflator.basis: CPI-U, all items, not seasonally adjusted, calendar-year mean of 12 monthly observations
deflator.note: October 2025 was never collected (2025 government shutdown; BLS said it could not retroactively gather it), so 2025 is the calendar-year mean of the 11 months that exist.

1923.why: The Revenue Act of 1921 granted a 25 percent reduction of the computed tax for the 1923 tax year, a one-time taxpayer credit layered on top of the 58% statutory ladder rather than a change to the bracket rate itself (43.5 = 58 x 0.75).
1923.source: Revenue Act of 1921, sec. 1200(a); IRS SOI Historical Table 23

1929.why: Congress voted a one-year, across-the-board reduction of the computed tax for 1929 in response to a Treasury surplus (24 = 25 x 0.96); the underlying bracket ladder was unchanged and the full 25% rate returned for 1930.
1929.source: Joint resolution of Dec. 16, 1929; IRS SOI Historical Table 23

1940.why: The Revenue Act of 1940 added a defense-preparedness surtax on top of the 79% ladder rate, most of it enacted after the tax year began, producing a blended published top of 81.1% rather than a clean 79 + surtax figure.
1940.source: Revenue Act of 1940, Title II (defense tax); IRS SOI Historical Table 23

1946.why: The Individual Income Tax Reduction Act of 1945 applied a percentage reduction credit to computed tax for 1946-1947 without rewriting the nominal 91% bracket ladder, so the published top (86.45%) is the ladder rate net of that credit.
1946.source: Individual Income Tax Reduction Act of 1945; IRS SOI Historical Table 23

1947.why: Same 1945 Act reduction credit as 1946; it applied to both the 1946 and 1947 tax years before the Revenue Act of 1948 replaced it with a larger cut.
1947.source: Individual Income Tax Reduction Act of 1945; IRS SOI Historical Table 23

1948.why: The Revenue Act of 1948 replaced the 1945 credit with a larger reduction formula (a combination of a tax-computation credit and a split-income provision for joint returns) for 1948-1949, again without changing the nominal 91% ladder.
1948.source: Revenue Act of 1948; IRS SOI Historical Table 23

1949.why: Same 1948 Act reduction formula as 1948; it covered both the 1948 and 1949 tax years before the Revenue Act of 1950 partially restored rates.
1949.source: Revenue Act of 1948; IRS SOI Historical Table 23

1950.why: The Revenue Act of 1950 (enacted September 1950) partially restored the pre-1948 rate structure but only for the remainder of the tax year, so 1950 carries a part-year blended top of 84.36% ahead of the full 91% that took effect for 1951.
1950.source: Revenue Act of 1950; IRS SOI Historical Table 23

1968.why: The Revenue and Expenditure Control Act of 1968 imposed a Vietnam-era income tax surcharge effective partway through the year, blending to an effective 7.5% surcharge on the 70% ladder for the full tax year (75.25 = 70 x 1.075).
1968.source: Revenue and Expenditure Control Act of 1968; IRS SOI Historical Table 23

1969.why: The 1968 surtax ran at a full 10% for all of 1969, cleanly scaling the 70% ladder (77.0 = 70 x 1.10).
1969.source: Revenue and Expenditure Control Act of 1968; IRS SOI Historical Table 23

1970.why: The surtax was cut to 5% and applied for only half of 1970 before expiring, blending to an effective 2.5% surcharge for the full tax year (71.75 = 70 x 1.025).
1970.source: Tax Reform Act of 1969 (surtax phase-out); IRS SOI Historical Table 23

1981.why: The Economic Recovery Tax Act of 1981 cut the top rate from 70% to 50% effective October 1, 1981; the published figure is the part-year blended rate for the nine months at 70% and three months at the newly enacted 50% schedule.
1981.source: Economic Recovery Tax Act of 1981; IRS SOI Historical Table 23

_meta.threshold_convention: Pre-modern rows (pre-2020) set a bracket's floor equal to the previous bracket's ceiling, as published; modern rows (2020 onward, and the fetched 2019 regression year) set the floor one dollar higher. Emitted as published in each source, not normalised across the boundary.
traps: Statutory is not effective. Nobody pays the top rate on their whole income, and the income threshold it applies at has moved enormously.
Ordinary income only. Capital gains have been taxed at separate, usually lower, rates for most of this period.

Surtaxes are INCLUDED in the published top rate for 1940 (a defense-preparedness surtax) and for 1968-1970 (the Vietnam-era income tax surtax). Every other year EXCLUDES surtaxes; see the adjustments list for exactly which years and by how much.
Excludes the alternative minimum tax, the phase-out of exemptions and deductions, and the 3.8% net investment income tax that has applied to high earners since 2013.
1981 shows 69.125%, the blended rate after a part-year cut when the Economic Recovery Tax Act of 1981 dropped the top rate from 70% to 50% partway through the year.
